questions.stem: For real x, let R(x) = (x − 2)/(x + 3). How many integers x satisfy −1 < R(x) < 0?
questions.explanation: By the sign of the factors, R is negative only on (−3, 2). There the lower bound is equivalent to 2x > −1, so 0 and 1 work.

questions.stem: What is the domain of the real function √[(x + 1)/(x − 2)] when x is restricted to −3 < x < 5?
questions.explanation: The signs agree on either side of the two critical values. Include the zero at −1 but not the pole at 2.

questions.stem: Let R(x) = (x² − 9)/(x² − 5x + 6). How many integers from −5 to 5 satisfy 0 < R(x) < 2?
questions.explanation: After excluding x = 2 and x = 3, R(x) is 1 + 5/(x − 2). For x > 2, R(x) < 2 requires x > 7. For x < 2, R(x) > 0 requires x < −3. Only −5 and −4 work, so the count is 2.

questions.stem: Let R(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2) with its natural domain. What is the least positive integer in its range that is not also in the range of R restricted to integers x ≤ 0?
questions.explanation: The function equals x + 2 except at x = 2. For integers x ≤ 0 the positive outputs are 1 and 2; output 3 is attained at x = 1.

questions.stem: For what integer a do (x + a)/(x − 1) and x/(x − 1) have opposite signs precisely on 0 < x < 3, apart from the point x = 1 where both are undefined?
questions.explanation: Away from 1, the product has the sign of x(x + a), so its negative interval lies strictly between 0 and −a. Hence −a = 3.

questions.stem: For how many integers x in [−4, 4] is 1/(x − 1) > 1/(x + 1)?
questions.explanation: On the common domain the difference is 2/(x² − 1), positive when |x| > 1. Three integers on each side qualify.

questions.stem: The inequalities (x − 1)/(x − 3) < 0 and (x − 2)/(x − 4) < 0 each define an interval. What is the length of the interval on which both hold?
questions.explanation: The first is negative precisely between its zero 1 and its pole 3. The second is negative between 2 and 4. Their common interval is (2, 3), of length 1.

questions.stem: Let h(x) = (x² − x)/(x² − 2x + 1). Which positive integer k gives exactly one negative integer x satisfying h(x) ≤ k/(k + 1)?
questions.explanation: On x < 0, h(x)=x/(x−1). Multiplying by x−1 reverses the inequality and yields x ≥ −k. There are exactly k qualifying negative integers.

questions.stem: For how many integers x is ((x − 7)(x − 2))/((x − 7)(x + 6)) ≤ 0?
questions.explanation:
x = 7 and x = −6 are excluded. Cancel x − 7 only after recording that restriction. The simplified ratio has opposite signs on top and bottom for −6 < x < 2, and is zero at x = 2. The excluded value 7 lies outside the interval. The integers run from -5 to 2.

Answer: 8.

questions.stem: For how many integers x is ((x − 13)(x − 10))/((x − 13)(x + 7)) ≤ 0?
questions.explanation:
x = 13 and x = −7 are excluded. Cancel x − 13 only after recording that restriction. The simplified ratio has opposite signs on top and bottom for −7 < x < 10, and is zero at x = 10. The excluded value 13 lies outside the interval. The integers run from -6 to 10.

Answer: 17.

questions.stem: For integer c, the parabola y = x² − 6x + c has no x-intercept while y = x² − 6x + c − 3 has two. How many c work?
questions.explanation: The two vertices have heights c−9 and c−12. The conditions are c > 9 and c < 12, leaving 10 and 11.

questions.stem: The quadratics x² − kx + 4 and x² + kx − 8 share a positive real root. What is k?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the equations at the common root gives kx = 6. Adding gives x² = 2. Thus k = 3√2.

questions.stem: There are two different values of k for which y = x² − kx + k is tangent to the x-axis. How far apart are the points of tangency?
questions.explanation: The discriminant k² − 4k vanishes when k = 0 or 4. At tangency the root is k/2, so the points are (0, 0) and (2, 0).

questions.stem: For which real k does x² + kx + k² have exactly one real zero?
questions.explanation: Its discriminant is −3k², which vanishes precisely at k=0; the double root is then 0.

questions.stem: The roots of x² − 7x + k = 0 are positive integers and their difference is prime. What is the greatest possible k?
questions.explanation: The unordered positive pairs summing to 7 are (1,6), (2,5), (3,4). Their differences are 5,3,1, so k can be 6 or 10, with maximum 10.

questions.stem: For real k the equation x² − 4x + k = 0 has real roots which differ by exactly 3. What are those roots' product and sum, respectively?
questions.explanation: The sum is 4. The squared difference is 16−4k=9, so the product is k=7/4.

questions.stem: For what value of k does the equation x² − (k + 2)x + 2k = 0 have just one distinct solution?
questions.explanation: The left side factors as (x − 2)(x − k). The two roots coincide only for k = 2.

questions.stem: The graph of y = x² − 2kx + 4 touches the line y = 2x only if k takes one of two values. What is the difference between those values?
questions.explanation: At tangency x²−2(k+1)x+4 has a double root, so (k+1)²=4 and the values are 1 and −3.

questions.stem: How many positive integers k make x² + 2(k − 11)x + 2(k − 11)² − 81 = 0 have distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
The discriminant is 4(81 − (k − 11)²), so |k − 11| < 9. Count integers from 3 to 19, inclusive.

Answer: 17.

questions.stem: How many positive integers k make x² + 2(k − 13)x + 2(k − 13)² − 16 = 0 have distinct real roots?
questions.explanation:
The discriminant is 4(16 − (k − 13)²), so |k − 13| < 4. Count integers from 10 to 16, inclusive.

Answer: 7.

questions.stem: Let f(x) = |x − 1|. What is the sum of the distinct roots of f(f(x)) = 0?
questions.explanation: The inner output must be 1. Thus x−1 is ±1, giving 0 and 2.

questions.stem: For which x is |x − 1| + |x + 1| at its minimum?
questions.explanation: This is the sum of the distances from x to −1 and 1. It is 2 on their joining interval and greater outside.

questions.stem: Let f(x) = |x| and g(x) = x² − 3. How many solutions does f(g(x)) = g(f(x)) + 2 have?
questions.explanation: The equation becomes |x² − 3| = x² − 1. If x² ≥ 3, it is impossible. Otherwise 3 − x² = x² − 1, so x² = 2 and both square roots work.

questions.stem: For f(x)=|x| and g(x)=x−2, what is the least possible value of f(g(x)) − g(f(x))?
questions.explanation: The difference is |x−2|−|x|+2. It is zero for x≥2, positive when x<2 by splitting at 0, and never negative by the triangle inequality.

questions.stem: How many real solutions does the equation ||x|−2| = |x−2| have that are strictly negative?
questions.explanation: For x<0 the left side is |x+2|, whereas |x−2| is strictly greater because x is closer to −2 than to 2.

questions.stem: The graph of y = |x² − 4| meets y = 3 four times. What is the distance between the leftmost and rightmost intersections?
questions.explanation: The equations are x²=7 or x²=1, so the outside pair are ±√7 and their separation is 2√7.

questions.stem: For f(x) = |x| − 1, how many real solutions does f(f(x)) = f(x) have?
questions.explanation: Let t = f(x), so t ≥ −1. If t ≥ 0 then |t| − 1 = t is impossible. In the remaining case −t − 1 = t gives t = −1/2, hence x = ±1/2.

questions.stem: Let f(x)=|x−2|+1. Within 0 ≤ x ≤ 3, what is the length of the interval on which f(x) < f(2x)?
questions.explanation: Squaring gives (x−2)²<(2x−2)², or x(3x−4)>0. Within the stated bounds this gives (4/3,3], of length 5/3.

questions.stem: Let f(x) = |x| − 2 and g(x) = |x| − 5. How many integers x in [−19, 19] make at least one of f(g(x)) and g(f(x)) zero?
questions.explanation:
The two equations give |x| = 5 ± 2 or |x| = 2 ± 5. Keeping only nonnegative possibilities gives magnitudes 7 and 3; they are distinct and nonzero. Each magnitude at most 19 contributes two integers.

Answer: 4.

questions.stem: Let f(x) = |x| − 13 and g(x) = |x| − 12. How many integers x in [−28, 28] make at least one of f(g(x)) and g(f(x)) zero?
questions.explanation:
The two equations give |x| = 12 ± 13 or |x| = 13 ± 12. Keeping only nonnegative possibilities gives magnitudes 25 and 1; they are distinct and nonzero. Each magnitude at most 28 contributes two integers.

Answer: 4.

questions.stem: How many distinct real x satisfy log₂(x+4) = log₄(2x+8)?
questions.explanation: The common domain is x>−4. With t=x+4, the equation becomes 2log₂t=1+log₂t, giving t=2.

questions.stem: For a real x both log₂(x−1) and log₂(5−x) are defined. What is the maximum of their sum?
questions.explanation: The product of the arguments is (x−1)(5−x)=4−(x−3)². It is largest at x=3, giving log₂4=2.

questions.stem: How many integers x make log₂[(x − 1)(x + 1)] < 3 true and defined?
questions.explanation: The logged expression must lie strictly between 0 and 8. Thus 1 < x² < 9, giving x = −2 and x = 2 only.

questions.stem: What is the least integer x satisfying log₃(x−2) + log₃(2) ≥ 2?
questions.explanation: The domain requires x>2. On it the bound is 2(x−2)≥9, so x≥13/2. The least integer is 7.

questions.stem: Which of the following values of a makes the real domain of log₂(x² − a) all real numbers?
questions.explanation: The least possible value of x²−a is −a at x=0. It must be strictly positive, so only the negative option works.

questions.stem: Let A = log₂3. What is log₈(9/2) in terms of A?
questions.explanation: Change the base to 2 by dividing log₂(9/2)=2A−1 by log₂8=3.

questions.stem: For real x, the equation log₃(x² − 2) = 2log₃(x − 2) has what solution set?
questions.explanation: The right side requires x > 2. Combining the logarithms gives x² − 2 = (x − 2)², or x = 3/2. This lies outside the common domain, so there is no solution.

questions.stem: Given that p>1 and log_p(x)+log_p(1/x)=0 for all positive x, which change always preserves the equation?
options: Replace one base by p² but leave the other unchanged.
Replace both arguments by their squares.
questions.explanation: Squaring both positive arguments doubles both logarithms, so their sum remains zero. A negative argument or x=0 is outside the domain.

questions.stem: Let x > 0. If the base-7 logarithm of [x(x + 1) + (16751)] equals 5, what is x?
questions.explanation:
Exponentiate to obtain x(x + 1) = 16807 − (16751) = 56. Subtract and factor: (x − 7)(x + 8) = 0. Only x = 7 is positive and its logarithm input is 16807.

Answer: 7.

questions.stem: Let x > 0. If the base-2 logarithm of [x(x + 13) + (-136)] equals 2, what is x?
questions.explanation:
Exponentiate to obtain x(x + 13) = 4 − (-136) = 140. Subtract and factor: (x − 7)(x + 20) = 0. Only x = 7 is positive and its logarithm input is 4.

Answer: 7.

questions.stem: In an arithmetic progression, a₂ + a₇ = 23. What is a₃ + a₄ + a₅ + a₆?
questions.explanation: Both a₃+a₆ and a₄+a₅ have index sum 9, just as a₂+a₇ does. Both equal 23.

questions.stem: Nine arithmetic terms have sum 45. Removing the fourth and sixth terms leaves what sum?
questions.explanation: The fifth term is the average, 5. The removed terms are symmetric about it and sum to 10.

questions.stem: In an arithmetic progression with twelve terms, the sums of the odd-position terms and even-position terms are 42 and 54 respectively. What is the fifth term?
questions.explanation: Each even-position term is its preceding odd-position term plus d, the common difference. The difference of sums is 6d = 12, so d = 2. The mean of the six odd-position terms is 7, halfway between the fifth and seventh terms, which are 4 apart. The fifth term is 5.

questions.stem: The positive multiples of 3 below 40 are written in increasing order. By how much does the sum of those at odd positions exceed the sum of those at even positions?
questions.explanation: Pair each even position with the next odd one, giving six differences of 3. The first term, 3, is unpaired.

questions.stem: An arithmetic progression has common difference 4. After three terms are inserted at equal spacing between each consecutive pair, the first nine terms of the new progression sum to 54. What was the first term?
questions.explanation: The inserted sequence has difference 1. Its average is 54/9=6, attained at position 5, four steps from its start.

questions.stem: The sum of the first n terms of a progression is 2n²−n. What is the difference between its seventh and fourth terms?
questions.explanation: Subtract consecutive partial sums to find aₙ=4n−3. Three steps increase it by 12.

questions.stem: An arithmetic progression with eight terms has the property that its odd-position terms sum to 22, and the sum of its first four terms is half that of its final four. What is the third term?
questions.explanation: Let the first term be a and common difference d. The equations are 4a + 12d = 22 and 2(4a + 6d) = 4a + 22d. The second gives 4a = 10d, so d = 1, a = 5/2 and the third term is 9/2.

questions.stem: Three arithmetic terms are the interior divider lengths of equally wide adjacent strips in a trapezium. The shortest divider is 6 and the longest is 10. What is the sum of the two parallel end lengths?
questions.explanation: The five parallel lengths are in arithmetic order. The end lengths have the same sum as the two outside divider lengths, 6+10.

questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence of 9 terms has sum 486. The last term exceeds the first by 96. By how much does the sum of the final 6 terms exceed the sum of the first 3 terms? Give a signed answer.
questions.explanation:
Divide 96 by 8 to get the common difference 12. The mean is 54, hence the first term is 6. The first 3 terms sum to 3(12+2×12)/2 = 54. Subtract twice that from 486.

Answer: 378.

questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence of 14 terms has sum 847. The last term exceeds the first by 117. By how much does the sum of the final 7 terms exceed the sum of the first 7 terms? Give a signed answer.
questions.explanation:
Divide 117 by 13 to get the common difference 9. The mean is 121/2, hence the first term is 2. The first 7 terms sum to 7(4+6×9)/2 = 203. Subtract twice that from 847.

Answer: 441.

questions.stem: A geometric series has first term 3 and ratio −1/2. What is the sum of its positive terms minus the sum of the magnitudes of its negative terms?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the magnitudes recovers the signed geometric sum, 3/(1+1/2)=2.

questions.stem: In a convergent geometric series of sum 10, the sum beyond term 4 is 5/8. What is the magnitude of the ratio?
questions.explanation: The tail divided by the full sum is r⁴=(5/8)/10=1/16, so |r|=1/2.

questions.stem: A convergent geometric series has positive first term, and its even-position terms sum to −2 while its odd-position terms sum to 5. What is the first term?
questions.explanation: The even-position terms are their immediate predecessors multiplied by r, so r = −2/5. The odd-position sum is a/(1 − r²), giving a = 5(1 − 4/25) = 21/5.

questions.stem: A square of area 16 is followed by squares whose side lengths are half the preceding side length. What is the sum of all areas except the first?
questions.explanation: Areas have ratio 1/4. The first included area is 4, giving 4/(1−1/4).

questions.stem: A convergent geometric series has nonzero first term a and sum 4a. Switching the signs of its even-position terms gives what sum?
questions.explanation: The original ratio is 3/4, since 1/(1−r)=4. The new ratio is −3/4, giving 4a/7.

questions.stem: An infinite geometric series has nonzero first term and positive ratio r<1. If every third term is discarded, what fraction of the original sum remains when r=1/2?
questions.explanation: The discarded series starts at ar² with ratio r³. As a fraction of the full sum this is r²/(1+r+r²)=1/7.

questions.stem: A convergent geometric series starts with 2 and has common ratio r < 0. The sum of the magnitudes of all its terms is three times its signed sum. What is r?
questions.explanation: The sum of magnitudes is 2/(1 + r), whereas the signed sum is 2/(1 − r). Their ratio is (1 − r)/(1 + r). Equating it to 3 gives r = −1/2.

questions.stem: A geometric series starts with 1 and its first three terms sum to 13/16. Its second term is greater than −1/2. What is its infinite sum?
questions.explanation: The ratio solves r²+r+3/16=0, so r=−1/4 or −3/4. The bound selects −1/4, yielding 4/5.

questions.stem: A geometric progression with 5 terms has positive integer ratio 2 and sum 279. A new sequence keeps the terms in odd positions and drops those in even positions (positions start at 1). What is the sum of the new sequence?
questions.explanation:
The original sum is first term × (2^5 − 1)/(2 − 1), so the first term is 9. The retained terms have ratio 4 and there are 3 of them. Sum this shorter progression.

Answer: 189.

questions.stem: A geometric progression with 5 terms has positive integer ratio 5 and sum 8591. A new sequence keeps the terms in odd positions and drops those in even positions (positions start at 1). What is the sum of the new sequence?
questions.explanation:
The original sum is first term × (5^5 − 1)/(5 − 1), so the first term is 11. The retained terms have ratio 25 and there are 3 of them. Sum this shorter progression.

Answer: 7161.

questions.stem: How many nonzero coefficients occur in (1+x)⁶+(1−x)⁶?
questions.explanation: Odd powers cancel. The degrees 0,2,4,6 each have a positive coefficient.

questions.stem: What is the constant term in the expansion of (x+2/x)⁴?
questions.explanation: Choose two x terms and two 2/x terms, giving C(4,2)·4=24.

questions.stem: The coefficient of x² in (1 + x)ⁿ equals the coefficient of x³, with n an integer greater than 3. What is the coefficient of x⁴?
questions.explanation: The ratio of the coefficients of x³ and x² is (n − 2)/3. Thus n = 5 and the required coefficient is C(5, 4) = 5.

questions.stem: In the expansion of (1+x)⁸, what is the sum of the coefficients on the even powers?
questions.explanation: Average the polynomial's values at 1 and −1 to cancel odd powers. The result is (256+0)/2.

questions.stem: Which two consecutive powers have equal coefficients in (1+2x)⁵?
questions.explanation: The consecutive ratio after xʲ is 2(5−j)/(j+1). It equals 1 at j=3.

questions.stem: In (1+x)ⁿ the coefficient of x² is three times that of x, with n a positive integer. What is n?
questions.explanation: The ratio C(n,2)/C(n,1) is (n−1)/2, which equals 3 at n=7.

questions.stem: The coefficient of x² in (1 − x)⁴(1 + kx) is −2. What is the coefficient of x³?
questions.explanation: The x² coefficient is 6 − 4k, giving k = 2. The x³ coefficient is −4 + 6k = 8.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of x⁵ in (1+x²)³(1+x)⁴?
questions.explanation: The contributing degree pairs are (2,3) and (4,1), giving 3·4+3·4.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of x^4 in (1 + 3x)^10(1 + 4x)?
questions.explanation:
Take either x^4 from the first factor and 1 from the last, or x^3 from the first and 4x from the last. The two contributions are 210×3^4 and 120×3^3×4.

Answer: 29970.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of x^5 in (1 + 4x)^11(1 + 8x)?
questions.explanation:
Take either x^5 from the first factor and 1 from the last, or x^4 from the first and 8x from the last. The two contributions are 462×4^5 and 330×4^4×8.

Answer: 1148928.

questions.stem: The line y=x+6 crosses y=x². What is the sum of the horizontal and vertical separations of their intersection points?
questions.explanation: The roots of x²−x−6 are −2 and 3, a horizontal gap of 5. The line has gradient 1, so its vertical gap is also 5.

questions.stem: The line through (−1,1) and (3,9) meets y=x² at both points. At how many points between them is the line three units above the parabola?
questions.explanation: The difference is (x+1)(3−x)=4−(x−1)². It equals 3 at 0 and 2.

questions.stem: The line through (2, 4) and (6, 36) cuts the parabola y = x² at those two points. On 2 ≤ x ≤ 6 what is the greatest vertical distance from the line to the parabola?
questions.explanation: The line minus the parabola is a quadratic with roots 2 and 6 and leading coefficient −1. It equals 4 − (x − 4)² and reaches its maximum 4 at the midpoint.

questions.stem: A line of gradient 6 cuts y=x² at two positive integer x-values. What is the largest possible horizontal gap?
questions.explanation: The roots have sum 6, so the extreme positive pair is 1 and 5.

questions.stem: The horizontal gap between intersections of y=x²−4x and y=5 is 6. After shifting the line down by 5, what is the horizontal gap?
questions.explanation: The shifted line is y=0. The parabola factors as x(x−4), with roots 0 and 4.

questions.stem: A chord of y=x² joins points with x-coordinates 1 and b>1. The chord cuts the y-axis at −5. What is b?
questions.explanation: The line minus parabola is −(x−1)(x−b), so the intercept is −b.

questions.stem: A line meets y = x² at x = p and x = q, where p < q. At x = (p + q)/2 the line is 9 units above the curve. What is q − p?
questions.explanation: Line minus curve is −(x − p)(x − q). At the midpoint this is (q − p)²/4. Since the separation is positive, q − p = 6.

questions.stem: Two chords of the parabola y=x² have the same midpoint x-coordinate 3. What must be equal for the two chords?
options: The distances from their midpoints to the x-axis.
The products of their endpoint x-coordinates.
questions.explanation: Between x=a and x=b the gradient is (b²−a²)/(b−a)=a+b. Both chords have a+b=6.

questions.stem: The curve y = 2x² intersects its secant through x = 15 and x = 14. What is the vertical distance between the secant and the curve at the midpoint of those two x-values?
questions.explanation:
The secant height halfway is the average of the two endpoint heights. Subtract the curve height 2((15 + 14)/2)². Simplifying this difference gives 2(15 − 14)²/4.

Answer: 1/2.

questions.stem: The curve y = 4x² intersects its secant through x = 14 and x = 3. What is the vertical distance between the secant and the curve at the midpoint of those two x-values?
questions.explanation:
The secant height halfway is the average of the two endpoint heights. Subtract the curve height 4((14 + 3)/2)². Simplifying this difference gives 4(14 − 3)²/4.

Answer: 121.

questions.stem: A circle of radius 5 has a horizontal chord of length 8. How far is the chord from the centre?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular bisects the chord. Its distance is √(5²−4²)=3.

questions.stem: The x-axis cuts x²+y²−6x−4y−7=0 in a chord. How long is it?
questions.explanation: At y=0, (x−3)²=16, so the two x-coordinates are four units either side of 3.

questions.stem: The line y = x cuts the circle x² + y² − 4x − 4y = 0 in two points. How far apart are they?
questions.explanation: Substituting y = x gives 2x(x − 4) = 0. The chord joins (0, 0) and (4, 4) and has length √(4² + 4²) = 4√2.

questions.stem: The line 3x+4y=10 cuts the circle x²+y²=29. What is the chord length?
questions.explanation: The distance from the origin to the line is 10/5=2. The half-chord is √(29−4)=5.

questions.stem: A diameter of a circle is 10. From a point on the circle two chords depart at a right angle, and the shorter is 6. What is the longer?
questions.explanation: The two chords and the diameter between their other ends form a right triangle. The longer chord is √(100−36).

questions.stem: A chord joins (0,0) to (6,8) on a circle whose centre lies on y=0. What is the radius?
questions.explanation: If the centre is (c,0), equating squared distances gives c²=(c−6)²+64, so c=25/3.

questions.stem: The line y = 3 intersects x² + y² = r² in a chord whose length equals r. What is r?
questions.explanation: Each half-chord is r/2 and the centre is 3 units away from the chord. Thus (r/2)² + 9 = r², giving the positive solution r = 2√3.

questions.stem: Two parallel chords, one through the centre and one 4 units from it, have lengths in the ratio 5:3. What is the radius?
questions.explanation: With radius r, the half-chords are r and 3r/5. Pythagoras gives r²−9r²/25=16.

questions.stem: A circle has centre (2, 4) and radius 25. Its intersections with y = 19 are A and B. What is |AB| divided by 1?
questions.explanation:
The line is 15 above the centre. Each endpoint lies horizontally √(25² − 15²) = 20 from the centre. Use both halves and divide the chord length 40 by 1.

Answer: 40.

questions.stem: A circle has centre (3, 2) and radius 20. Its intersections with y = 14 are A and B. What is |AB| divided by 2?
questions.explanation:
The line is 12 above the centre. Each endpoint lies horizontally √(20² − 12²) = 16 from the centre. Use both halves and divide the chord length 32 by 2.

Answer: 16.

questions.stem: Where do the tangents to y=x³ at x=−1 and x=1 meet?
questions.explanation: Both have gradient 3, but their intercepts are 2 and −2. They are distinct parallel lines.

questions.stem: For y=x², a tangent goes through (0,−9). What is its positive possible gradient?
questions.explanation: A tangent at x=t has equation y=2tx−t². Set t²=9 and take t=3 for a positive gradient.

questions.stem: The tangents to y = 1/x at x = 1 and x = 2 intersect at T. The tangent at x = 1 meets the x-axis at A, and the tangent at x = 2 meets it at B. What is the area of triangle ATB?
questions.explanation: The tangents are y = 2 − x and y = 1 − x/4. Their intersection has x = 4/3 and y = 2/3. Their x-axis intercepts are 2 and 4, so the area is half of 2 times 2/3.

questions.stem: The tangent to y=√x at x=4 intersects the y-axis. What is the intercept?
questions.explanation: The point is (4,2) and the gradient 1/4, so the intercept is 2−4/4=1.

questions.stem: At x=1 the tangents to y=x² and y=ax³ are perpendicular. What is a?
questions.explanation: Their gradients are 2 and 3a. Perpendicularity gives product −1.

questions.stem: The tangent to y=x² at x=2 and the tangent to y=x³ at x=1 intersect. What is the x-coordinate of their intersection?
questions.explanation: Their equations are y=4x−4 and y=3x−2. Equating gives x=2.

questions.stem: A tangent to y = x² at a positive x-coordinate meets the tangent at x = −1 on the y-axis. What is the gradient of the first tangent?
questions.explanation: The tangent at x = a has y-intercept −a². To coincide with the intercept −1 of the other tangent, a must be 1 (since a > 0). The gradient is 2a = 2.

questions.stem: How many tangents to y=x³ pass through the origin?
questions.explanation: A tangent at t has intercept t³−3t³=−2t³. This vanishes only at t=0.

questions.stem: The tangents to y = 3x² at x = 4 and x = 10 intersect at T. What is the x-coordinate of T?
questions.explanation:
The tangent at x = t has slope 6t and intercept −3t². Equate the lines to get x = (10² − 4²)/(2(10 − 4)). Cancel the difference using the difference of squares.

Answer: 7.

questions.stem: The tangents to y = 6x² at x = 3 and x = 9 intersect at T. What is the x-coordinate of T?
questions.explanation:
The tangent at x = t has slope 12t and intercept −6t². Equate the lines to get x = (9² − 3²)/(2(9 − 3)). Cancel the difference using the difference of squares.

Answer: 6.

questions.stem: The cubic y=x³−12x has two stationary points. What is the vertical distance between them?
questions.explanation: The derivative vanishes at ±2. The cubic takes values ±16 there, giving distance 32.

questions.stem: The graph of f(x)=x³−3x+2 is shifted up by k. Which k places its local maximum on the x-axis?
questions.explanation: The derivative changes from positive to negative at −1, where f is 4.

questions.stem: The cubic f(x) = x³ − 3x + c has two stationary points. At the local maximum, the value of f is twice the value at the local minimum. What is c?
questions.explanation: The derivative vanishes at −1 and 1. Its sign changes from positive to negative at −1, giving a maximum c + 2, and from negative to positive at 1, giving a minimum c − 2. Thus c + 2 = 2(c − 2) and c = 6.

questions.stem: For which k does the cubic y=x³−3kx have no stationary point?
questions.explanation: The derivative vanishes exactly when x²=k. This has no real solution precisely for negative k.

questions.stem: A monic cubic has a stationary point at x=0 and another at x=2, and passes through (0,0). What is its value at 2?
questions.explanation: Its derivative is 3x(x−2), so f(x)=x³−3x² from f(0)=0.

questions.stem: The cubic x³−3x+c has a positive local maximum and a negative local minimum. Which c satisfy both?
questions.explanation: The values at −1 and 1 are c+2 and c−2. For opposite strict signs c lies between −2 and 2.

questions.stem: The cubic y = x³ + ax² + bx has stationary points at x = 1 and x = 3. What is the mean of its two stationary values?
questions.explanation: Its derivative is 3(x − 1)(x − 3), so a = −6 and b = 9. The values at 1 and 3 are 4 and 0, giving mean 2.

questions.stem: For f(x)=x³−3x, at which x besides the local minimum does f take the local minimum value?
questions.explanation: The minimum occurs at 1 and has value −2. Then f(x)+2=(x−1)²(x+2), giving the other x=−2.

questions.stem: By how much does the local maximum value of f(x) = 2x³ − 30x² + 126x + 12 exceed its local minimum value?
questions.explanation:
Differentiate: f′(x) = 6(x − 3)(x − 7). The sign changes + to − at 3 and − to + at 7. On putting x = 3 + t, the nonconstant part becomes 2t³ − 3(4)t². Going from t = 0 to 4 lowers the value by (4)³.

Answer: 64.

questions.stem: By how much does the local maximum value of f(x) = 2x³ − 39x² + 132x + 11 exceed its local minimum value?
questions.explanation:
Differentiate: f′(x) = 6(x − 2)(x − 11). The sign changes + to − at 2 and − to + at 11. On putting x = 2 + t, the nonconstant part becomes 2t³ − 3(9)t². Going from t = 0 to 9 lowers the value by (9)³.

Answer: 729.

questions.stem: The signed integral of y=x−2 over [0,5] is 5/2. What is the total area between the line and axis?
questions.explanation: The negative triangular area is 2. Converting its contribution from −2 to +2 adds 4 to the signed integral.

questions.stem: The area under y=x² between x=0 and x=3 is A. What is the area above y=−2x² between x=0 and x=3 up to the axis?
questions.explanation: The new vertical distance from the axis is 2x² at each x, so the area doubles.

questions.stem: The area below the x-axis and above y = x² − 4, between x = 0 and x = 2, equals the area above the x-axis and below the horizontal line y = h between the same vertical boundaries. What is h?
questions.explanation: The first area is the integral of 4 − x² from 0 to 2, equal to 16/3. The second is the area 2h of a rectangle. Therefore h = 8/3.

questions.stem: For what positive b is the signed integral of 2x−3 from 0 to b equal to zero?
questions.explanation: The integral is b²−3b. Apart from b=0 its only zero is b=3.

questions.stem: The graph of y=|x−1| is shifted down one unit. What is the area between the new graph and the axis over [0,2]?
questions.explanation: It is nonpositive on [0,2], and forms a triangle of base 2 and height 1.

questions.stem: A continuous function is negative throughout (0,4). The area bounded by its graph, the x-axis and the lines x=0 and x=4 is 12. What is the signed integral of 2f(x)+3 over [0,4]?
questions.explanation: The signed integral of f is −12, so the transformed integral is −24+12=−12.

questions.stem: The signed integral of y = x(x − 2)(x − 4) from 0 to 4 is zero. What is the total area between the curve and the x-axis on that interval?
questions.explanation: The curve is above the axis on (0, 2) and below on (2, 4). The integral on (0, 2) is 4. Because the signed integral is zero, both regions have area 4, giving total area 8.

questions.stem: How much does the area between y=x²−4 and the axis on [−2,2] exceed the corresponding area for y=x²−1 on [−1,1]?
questions.explanation: Integrate each positive distance below the axis: 32/3 and 4/3. Subtract them.

questions.stem: What is the exact area between y = 4(x − 5)(x − 8) and the x-axis for 5 ≤ x ≤ 8?
questions.explanation:
The curve is nonpositive here. Let t = x − 5, so y = 4(t² − 3t). Integrate its negative from 0 to 3: 4[3t²/2 − t³/3] at the upper limit gives the area.

Answer: 18.

questions.stem: What is the exact area between y = 8(x − 9)(x − 11) and the x-axis for 9 ≤ x ≤ 11?
questions.explanation:
The curve is nonpositive here. Let t = x − 9, so y = 8(t² − 2t). Integrate its negative from 0 to 2: 8[2t²/2 − t³/3] at the upper limit gives the area.

Answer: 32/3.

questions.stem: On 0≤x<2π, how many solutions of sin²x=3/4 also have sin x<0?
questions.explanation: The negative branch has value −√3/2, achieved once in each lower quadrant.

questions.stem: What is the range of 4sin²x−2 over all real x?
questions.explanation: The square fills [0,1]. Multiplying by four and translating by −2 gives [−2,2].

questions.stem: On 0 ≤ x < 2π, how many solutions of sin²x = 1/4 also satisfy cos x < 0?
questions.explanation: The sine must be 1/2 or −1/2. The cosine is negative in the second and third quadrants; each of those quadrants contains one of the required sine values.

questions.stem: On 0≤x≤π, what is the sum of the two solutions of sin²x=1/9?
questions.explanation: On this interval sin x≥0 and the two solutions are symmetric about π/2.

questions.stem: What is sin⁴x−cos⁴x when cos(2x)=1/3?
questions.explanation: Factor as (sin²x−cos²x)(sin²x+cos²x)=−cos(2x).

questions.stem: For 0≤x<2π how many x satisfy sin²x=sin x?
questions.explanation: The sine is 0 at 0 and π, and 1 at π/2.

questions.stem: How many solutions does sin²x·cos x = cos²x have on 0 ≤ x < 2π?
questions.explanation: Factor as cos x(sin²x − cos x) = 0. One branch gives cos x = 0, with two solutions. On the other branch c = cos x satisfies c² + c − 1 = 0. Only the positive root is in [−1, 1], and it gives two more solutions.

questions.stem: What is the greatest value of sin²x cos²x for real x?
questions.explanation: Let t=sin²x. The product is t(1−t), whose maximum is 1/4 at t=1/2.

questions.stem: In 0 ≤ x < 2160° how many solutions are there to 3sin²(x) = 2?
questions.explanation:
sin(x) = ±√(2/3). The magnitude is strictly between 0 and 1. Each nonzero value in (−1, 1) occurs twice per full turn of 360°, and there are 6 full turns.

Answer: 24.

questions.stem: In 0 ≤ x < 1080° how many solutions are there to 4sin²(x) = 2?
questions.explanation:
sin(x) = ±√(2/4). The magnitude is strictly between 0 and 1. Each nonzero value in (−1, 1) occurs twice per full turn of 360°, and there are 3 full turns.

Answer: 12.

questions.stem: What is the maximum of cos x−cos²x on 0≤x≤π?
questions.explanation: Set c=cos x. Then c−c²=1/4−(c−1/2)², with equality possible.

questions.stem: For what k does cos(2x)=k have exactly three solutions on [0,2π]?
questions.explanation: Interior levels have four intersections; level −1 has two minima and level 1 has the two endpoints and one interior maximum.

questions.stem: Let f(x) = 1 + 2cos x − 2cos²x on 0 ≤ x ≤ π/2. What is the difference between its maximum and minimum values?
questions.explanation: Put c = cos x, which fills [0, 1]. The expression is 3/2 − 2(c − 1/2)², so the maximum is 3/2 at c = 1/2 and the minimum 1 at either endpoint.

questions.stem: What is the difference between the largest and smallest values of 3cos x−1 for π/3≤x≤π?
questions.explanation: Cosine decreases across this interval and runs from 1/2 to −1, so scaling the spread gives 9/2.

questions.stem: Which value of x maximises cos(2x)+2cos x on [π/2,π]?
questions.explanation: For c=cos x in [−1,0], the expression is 2c(c+1)−1, which equals −1 at both ends and is less inside.

questions.stem: What is cos(2x) at a point where 2cos x−cos(2x) takes its maximum?
questions.explanation: With c=cos x, the expression is 1+2c−2c², maximised at c=1/2. Then 2c²−1=−1/2.

questions.stem: What is the minimum of 2cos x + cos(2x) on π/3 ≤ x ≤ π/2?
questions.explanation: With c = cos x, the expression is 2c² + 2c − 1. It increases with c throughout [0, 1/2], so the minimum is −1 at c = 0, attained at x = π/2.

questions.stem: How many roots does cos x=1/2 have on −π/3<x≤5π/3?
questions.explanation: The first endpoint is excluded, but π/3 and 5π/3 are in the interval.

questions.stem: How many solutions does 3cos(2x) = -1cos(x) + (4) have for 0° ≤ x < 2520°?
questions.explanation:
Use cos(2x) = 2cos²(x) − 1. With u = cos(x), the equation becomes (u − 1)(6u + 7) = 0. The root 1 contributes once per turn. The root −7/6 contributes twice if strictly inside (−1, 1), once at −1, and not at all below −1. There are 7 full turns.

Answer: 7.

questions.stem: How many solutions does 2cos(2x) = -5cos(x) + (7) have for 0° ≤ x < 2520°?
questions.explanation:
Use cos(2x) = 2cos²(x) − 1. With u = cos(x), the equation becomes (u − 1)(4u + 9) = 0. The root 1 contributes once per turn. The root −9/4 contributes twice if strictly inside (−1, 1), once at −1, and not at all below −1. There are 7 full turns.

Answer: 7.

questions.stem: Two fair dice are rolled. Given that the sum is 7, what is the probability the first die shows a prime?
questions.explanation: There is exactly one matching second die for each first result; 2,3,5 are prime.

questions.stem: Two cards are drawn without replacement from cards numbered 1 to 7. Given that neither is a multiple of 3, what is the probability both are odd?
questions.explanation: The eligible cards are 1,2,4,5,7. Three are odd, so the count ratio is C(3,2)/C(5,2).

questions.stem: A fair coin is flipped three times. Given that at most one pair of consecutive flips has the same result, what is the probability that the first and last results are equal?
questions.explanation: Only HHH and TTT have two equal consecutive pairs. In the six eligible outcomes, only HTH and THT have equal end results. That gives 2/6.

questions.stem: Three fair coin tosses include exactly two heads. What is the probability the two heads are adjacent?
questions.explanation: HTH, HHT and THH are equally likely, with adjacency in the latter two.

questions.stem: Two distinct numbers are picked uniformly from 1 to 5. Given the smaller is 2, what is the probability the sum is odd?
questions.explanation: The larger is equally likely to be 3,4 or 5. Adding 2 preserves its parity.

questions.stem: A fair die is rolled twice. Given that the second reading exceeds the first, what is the probability they differ by exactly one?
questions.explanation: There are C(6,2)=15 increasing pairs, of which five are consecutive.

questions.stem: One of the unordered pairs of distinct numbers from 1 through 5 is picked uniformly. Given that exactly one of its numbers is even, what is the probability that the smaller number is even?
questions.explanation: The even number can be 2 or 4 and the odd number 1, 3 or 5, giving six pairs. With even number 2, two odd numbers are greater; with even number 4, one is greater. Thus three pairs qualify.

questions.stem: An ordered pair is chosen uniformly from {0,1,2,3}². Given the product is not zero, what is the probability the two entries are equal?
questions.explanation: Both entries must be in {1,2,3}. Of the nine equally likely pairs, three are on the diagonal.

questions.stem: A bag has 8 blue and 4 gold tokens. Two distinct tokens are drawn uniformly without replacement. Given at least one is blue, what is the probability both are blue?
questions.explanation:
Restrict to pairs containing blue. There are 28 blue-blue pairs and 32 mixed pairs. Divide the first count by their sum.

Answer: 7/15.

questions.stem: A bag has 9 blue and 7 gold tokens. Two distinct tokens are drawn uniformly without replacement. Given at least one is blue, what is the probability both are blue?
questions.explanation:
Restrict to pairs containing blue. There are 36 blue-blue pairs and 63 mixed pairs. Divide the first count by their sum.

Answer: 4/11.

questions.stem: How many odd three-digit integers can be formed from 1,2,3 if digits may repeat but neighbours must differ?
questions.explanation: Choose the final digit in two ways. Each digit before it has two choices different from its neighbour.

questions.stem: How many three-digit positive integers have strictly increasing digits from {0,1,2,3,4,5}?
questions.explanation: Zero cannot appear because in increasing order it would be first. Each 3-element subset of the five remaining digits has exactly one order.

questions.stem: How many four-digit positive integers use digits 0, 1, 2 and 3 exactly once each and are even?
questions.explanation: An even number ends in 0 or 2. Ending in 0 leaves 3! = 6 arrangements. Ending in 2 leaves two choices for the nonzero first digit and two orders for the middle digits, giving another 4.

questions.stem: How many three-digit positive integers use just digits 1 and 2, use both, and have an even digit sum?
questions.explanation: An even sum requires zero or two copies of 1. Both digits occur, so choose which one of three places is the 2.

questions.stem: How many palindromic four-digit positive integers are even?
questions.explanation: The first digit equals the last and must be one of 2,4,6,8. Either middle digit can be any of the ten digits but determines the other.

questions.stem: How many even integers strictly between 20 and 50 have two different digits?
questions.explanation: The even integers run from 22 to 48, giving 14 values. Exclude 22 and 44, leaving 12.

questions.stem: Four-digit strings use only 1 and 2. How many strings have exactly two odd digits with at least one digit between them?
questions.explanation: The positions of the two 1s determine the string. There are six unordered pairs of positions, three of which are adjacent. The three nonadjacent choices are (1, 3), (1, 4), and (2, 4).

questions.stem: A code contains the digits 0,1,2,3 in some order. How many codes have both even digits before both odd digits?
questions.explanation: Order 0,2 in the first two positions and 1,3 in the last two: 2!·2!.

questions.stem: Codes have length 2 using digits 5 through 7, with repetitions allowed. How many codes have an even sum of their digits?
questions.explanation:
There are 1 even and 2 odd choices. The total count is 3^2. The even count minus the odd count is (1 − 2)^2: expand the product, giving each odd digit a minus sign. Add the two counts equations and halve.

Answer: 5.

questions.stem: Codes have length 3 using digits 3 through 4, with repetitions allowed. How many codes have an even sum of their digits?
questions.explanation:
There are 1 even and 1 odd choices. The total count is 2^3. The even count minus the odd count is (1 − 1)^3: expand the product, giving each odd digit a minus sign. Add the two counts equations and halve.

Answer: 4.

questions.stem: Among integers 1 to 60, how many are divisible by 6 and by neither 4 nor 9?
questions.explanation: Of ten multiples of 6, five are multiples of 12, three of 18, and one of both. Thus 10−5−3+1=3.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the integers from 1 to 20 divisible by 3 or 5, including those divisible by both?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 3 sum to 63 and those of 5 sum to 50. Subtract 15, counted twice.

questions.stem: An integer chosen uniformly from 1 to 36 is known to be divisible by 4 or 6, or both. What is the probability it is divisible by just one of them?
questions.explanation: Nine are divisible by 4 and six by 6. The three multiples of 12 lie in both counts, so 12 integers meet the given condition, of which 12 − 3 = 9 meet exactly one test.

questions.stem: Which positive integer is the fifth smallest multiple of 4 that is not a multiple of 6?
questions.explanation: The qualifying list begins 4,8,16,20,28. Multiples of 12 are skipped.

questions.stem: How many pairs of consecutive integers in {1,…,20} have one member divisible by 3 and the other by 4?
questions.explanation: Checking neighbours of 4,8,12,16,20 gives (3,4), (8,9), (15,16).

questions.stem: Among the positive divisors of 48, how many are divisible by exactly one of 4 and 6?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 4 among the divisors are 4,8,12,16,24,48. Only 6 among the multiples of 6 is not in that list. Removing overlaps leaves 4,8,16 and 6.

questions.stem: From 1 to N inclusive, exactly six integers are divisible by 3 but not by 6. Which is the greatest possible N?
questions.explanation: The eligible integers are 3, 9, 15, 21, 27, 33 and then 39. The largest N before including the seventh is 38.

questions.stem: In every block of 12 consecutive integers, what fraction is divisible by neither 3 nor 4?
questions.explanation: There are four multiples of 3, three of 4, and one shared multiple of 12. Exclude their union of six.

questions.stem: An integer is chosen uniformly from 1 to 91 inclusive. What is the probability that it is divisible by exactly one of 9 and 7?
questions.explanation:
The counts of multiples are 10 and 13. The common multiples are multiples of 63, of which there are 1. These were counted twice and must contribute zero. Divide the remaining count by 91.

Answer: 3/13.

questions.stem: An integer is chosen uniformly from 1 to 66 inclusive. What is the probability that it is divisible by exactly one of 6 and 9?
questions.explanation:
The counts of multiples are 11 and 7. The common multiples are multiples of 18, of which there are 3. These were counted twice and must contribute zero. Divide the remaining count by 66.

Answer: 2/11.

questions.stem: The function f satisfies f(t)≠0 exactly when 2<t<8. How many positive integers n satisfy f(12/n)≠0?
questions.explanation: For positive n the condition is 3/2<n<6, admitting 2,3,4,5.

questions.stem: A function f has f(x)>3 precisely when x<−2 or x>3. How many integers in [−5,5] satisfy f(x+1)>3?
questions.explanation: The shift gives x<−3 or x>2. The integers are −5,−4,3,4,5.

questions.stem: A function f has value 1 exactly when 0 ≤ its input ≤ 2. What is the total length of the intervals on which f(x² − 1) = 1?
questions.explanation: The condition is 0 ≤ x² − 1 ≤ 2, or 1 ≤ x² ≤ 3. The intervals are [−√3, −1] and [1, √3], each of length √3 − 1.

questions.stem: The domain of g is [−1,4]. What is the domain of g(√x)?
questions.explanation: The square root requires x≥0; its allowed values are 0 through 4. Squaring gives x≤16.

questions.stem: A function f is positive exactly on [1,4]. What is the length of the set of x for which both f(x) and f(5−2x) are positive?
questions.explanation: The second condition gives 1/2≤x≤2. Its intersection with [1,4] is [1,2].

questions.stem: The function g equals 2 precisely on (−3,−1). How many integer x satisfy g(−|x|)=2?
questions.explanation: The condition is 1<|x|<3, so x=±2.

questions.stem: A function f is negative precisely on (1, 5). On which of these intervals is f(3 − 2x) negative?
questions.explanation: The input must satisfy 1 < 3 − 2x < 5. Subtract 3 and divide by −2, reversing both inequalities, to get −1 < x < 1.

questions.stem: If f exceeds zero precisely on (0,1), which x make f((x−1)(x−3)) positive?
questions.explanation: The input is (x−2)²−1. Requiring it strictly between 0 and 1 gives 1<|x−2|<√2.

questions.stem: A function f is positive precisely for 2 ≤ t ≤ 8 (its input is t). How many integer values of x make f(25 − x) positive?
questions.explanation:
The constraint is 2 ≤ 25 − x ≤ 8. Rearranging reverses both inequalities: 17 ≤ x ≤ 23. Count both endpoints.

Answer: 7.

questions.stem: A function f is positive precisely for 8 ≤ t ≤ 9 (its input is t). How many integer values of x make f(16 − x) positive?
questions.explanation:
The constraint is 8 ≤ 16 − x ≤ 9. Rearranging reverses both inequalities: 7 ≤ x ≤ 8. Count both endpoints.

Answer: 2.

questions.stem: If P leaves remainder x+4 on division by x²−4, what is its remainder on division by x+2?
questions.explanation: Since x+2 divides x²−4, evaluating the remainder at −2 gives P(−2)=2.

questions.stem: A polynomial is divisible by x−1 and has remainder 6 on division by x−3. Its remainder on division by (x−1)(x−3) has what gradient?
questions.explanation: The remainder must pass through (1,0) and (3,6). Its gradient is the rise over a run of two.

questions.stem: A polynomial P has remainder 1 on division by x − 1 and remainder 5 on division by x − 3. Which linear divisor x − k gives remainder 7 when dividing the linear remainder of P modulo (x − 1)(x − 3)?
questions.explanation: The linear remainder passes through (1, 1) and (3, 5), so it is 2x − 1. Its value is 7 at x = 4. Thus the divisor is x − 4.

questions.stem: For what k does x³+kx+2 leave the same remainder on division by x−1 and x+1?
questions.explanation: The remainders 3+k and 1−k must be equal.

questions.stem: When a polynomial is divided by x²+1 its remainder is 3x−2. What is the remainder when x times the polynomial is divided by the same divisor?
questions.explanation: The new remainder comes from 3x²−2x. Replace x² by −1 modulo x²+1.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when x⁶+2x⁴+x² is divided by x²+1?
questions.explanation: Factor as x²(x²+1)², so the divisor is an exact factor.

questions.stem: A polynomial P leaves remainder 2x + 3 on division by (x − 1)². What must P′(1) equal?
questions.explanation: Write P(x) = (x − 1)²Q(x) + 2x + 3. Both terms obtained by differentiating the product still contain a factor of x − 1, so they vanish at x = 1 and leave P′(1) = 2.

questions.stem: The polynomial P(x)=x³+2x leaves remainders R₁,R₂ when divided by x−a,x+a respectively. If a>0 and R₁−R₂=24, what is a?
questions.explanation: Oddness gives R₁−R₂=2a³+4a. This is strictly increasing for positive a and equals 24 at a=2.

questions.stem: A polynomial P satisfies P(8) = 13 and P(12) = 15. Its remainder on division by (x − 8)(x − 12) is R(x). Find R(20).
questions.explanation:
The remainder is at most linear. At each root of the divisor the quotient term vanishes, so R passes through (8, 13) and (12, 15). Its slope is (15 − 13)/(12 − 8) = 1/2. Start at x = 8 and move 12 units.

Answer: 19.

questions.stem: A polynomial P satisfies P(11) = 15 and P(10) = 10. Its remainder on division by (x − 11)(x − 10) is R(x). Find R(23).
questions.explanation:
The remainder is at most linear. At each root of the divisor the quotient term vanishes, so R passes through (11, 15) and (10, 10). Its slope is (10 − 15)/(10 − 11) = 5. Start at x = 11 and move 12 units.

Answer: 75.

questions.stem: Two adjacent bins have widths 2 and 4 and equal frequency. What fraction of the sum of their heights comes from the taller bar?
questions.explanation: Equal areas make the narrower bar twice as high, so its share is 2/(2+1).

questions.stem: Classes [0,2) and [2,8) have frequencies 12 and 6. What is their combined midpoint estimate of the mean?
questions.explanation: The representative points are 1 and 5. Their weighted mean is (12+30)/18.

questions.stem: A histogram has two bars of equal height over the classes 0 ≤ t < 2 and 2 ≤ t < 6. The upper class is split at t = 4, and the new bar over 4 ≤ t < 6 is given twice its original height, while all other heights stay unchanged. What is the resulting midpoint estimate of the mean?
questions.explanation: Take the original common height as 1, since overall scaling cancels. The frequencies are 2, 2 and 4, and the midpoints are 1, 3 and 5. The weighted mean is (2 + 6 + 20)/8 = 7/2.

questions.stem: A histogram of 20 scores has classes [0,4) and [4,8). Its midpoint estimate of the mean is 5. How many scores are in the second class?
questions.explanation: For n scores with midpoint 6 and 20−n with midpoint 2, the estimated total is 40+4n=100.

questions.stem: A single class interval [0,8) at one fixed density is split into [0,2) and [2,8), both retaining that density. By how much does its midpoint mean estimate change?
questions.explanation: The new midpoints 1 and 5 receive weights 2 and 6, so their weighted mean is still 4.

questions.stem: At the midpoints, a grouped estimate of the mean is 14. Every class boundary is increased by 3 and every class frequency doubled. What is the new estimate?
questions.explanation: Doubling all weights cancels between numerator and denominator. Every midpoint increases by 3, so the estimate becomes 17.

questions.stem: A histogram of 18 values has classes [0, 1) and [1, 3). The second bar is four times the height of the first. What is the midpoint estimate of the mean?
questions.explanation: Because the second class is twice as wide and four times as tall, its frequency is eight times the first. The mean therefore is (1/2 + 8·2)/9 = 11/6.

questions.stem: Only two classes, [0,2) and [2,6), occur in a histogram, each with nonzero frequency. Which statement about the true mean is forced?
questions.explanation: All observations are below 6 and at least 0, and the upper class supplies positive observations. Any narrower proposed bound can fail depending on the class frequencies and locations.

questions.stem: A histogram uses intervals [0, 4), [4, 12), [12, 20) and respective frequency densities 2, 11/8, 7/2. Using class midpoints, what is the estimate of the mean?
questions.explanation:
Area gives frequency: 8, 11, 28. The midpoints are 2, 8, 16. Form their frequency-weighted sum and divide by 47.

Answer: 552/47.

questions.stem: A histogram uses intervals [0, 6), [6, 11), [11, 16) and respective frequency densities 13/6, 7/5, 12/5. Using class midpoints, what is the estimate of the mean?
questions.explanation:
Area gives frequency: 13, 7, 12. The midpoints are 3, 17/2, 27/2. Form their frequency-weighted sum and divide by 32.

Answer: 521/64.

questions.stem: The diagonals of a parallelogram meet at O. A point P bisects OA, where A is a vertex. What fraction of the parallelogram is triangle POB when B is the next vertex after A?
questions.explanation: The diagonals give four equal areas. With base on the same diagonal, POB has half the base of AOB and the same height.

questions.stem: A triangle is cut by a line parallel to its base so that the smaller triangle has one third of the original height. What is the ratio of the trapezium's area to the smaller triangle's?
questions.explanation: Similar lengths scale by 1/3 and areas by 1/9. The area ratio is therefore (1−1/9)/(1/9).

questions.stem: The curves y = x² and y = x enclose an area A. On the same x-interval, the line y = 1 is above both curves. What is the ratio of the area between y = 1 and y = x² to A?
questions.explanation: The first region runs from x = 0 to x = 1 and has area ∫₀¹(x − x²) dx = 1/6. The other area is ∫₀¹(1 − x²) dx = 2/3, giving ratio 4.

questions.stem: A line from A to D on BC cuts triangle ABC into two triangles with areas in the ratio 2:5. If BC=21, what is the shorter of BD and DC?
questions.explanation: Their altitudes from A agree, so dividing BC in the ratio 2:5 gives shorter length 21·2/7.

questions.stem: A circle is inscribed in a square, and a second square is inscribed in that circle. What fraction of the outer square's area is inside the inner square?
questions.explanation: The inner diagonal equals the outer side. A square with diagonal d has area d²/2.

questions.stem: A triangle has vertices (0,0), (8,0), (2,5). The point (2,2) is joined to each vertex. What fraction of the original area is in the triangle containing the base on the x-axis?
questions.explanation: The base remains 8, but the height is 2 instead of 5.

questions.stem: For m > 0, let A(m) be the area enclosed by y = mx and y = x². Given that A(m) : A(m + 1) = 8 : 27, what is m?
questions.explanation: The curves meet at x = 0 and x = m. The integral of mx − x² over [0, m] is m³/6. Taking the cube root of the ratio gives m/(m + 1) = 2/3, so m = 2.

questions.stem: The segment from the midpoint of one leg of a right triangle to the midpoint of its hypotenuse has length 4. What fraction of the triangle's area is on the side of this segment containing the right-angle vertex?
questions.explanation: The midpoint segment is parallel to the other leg. It cuts off a similar triangle with half the linear scale and a quarter of the area.

questions.stem: The curves y = 3x² + 81 and y = 36x enclose a region. A second region lies between the curves from their rightmost intersection to x = 21. What is the ratio of the second area to the first?
questions.explanation:
Subtract the line height from the parabola height: 3(x − 3)(x − 9). With u = (x − 9)/6, the difference is 108u(u + 1). The first region corresponds to −1 ≤ u ≤ 0 and has negative signed integral −1/6 of u(u + 1); the second runs from 0 to 2 and has integral 2³/3 + 2²/2. The common scale factors cancel. Divide the latter integral by 1/6.

Answer: 28.

questions.stem: The curves y = 5x² + 520 and y = 105x enclose a region. A second region lies between the curves from their rightmost intersection to x = 18. What is the ratio of the second area to the first?
questions.explanation:
Subtract the line height from the parabola height: 5(x − 8)(x − 13). With u = (x − 13)/5, the difference is 125u(u + 1). The first region corresponds to −1 ≤ u ≤ 0 and has negative signed integral −1/6 of u(u + 1); the second runs from 0 to 1 and has integral 1³/3 + 1²/2. The common scale factors cancel. Divide the latter integral by 1/6.

Answer: 5.

questions.stem: The roots of x²−5x+3=0 are r and s. What is the sum of the roots of (2x+1)²−5(2x+1)+3=0?
questions.explanation: The new roots are (r−1)/2 and (s−1)/2. Their sum is (5−2)/2.

questions.stem: If a and b solve x²−3x−2=0, what is a/b+b/a?
questions.explanation: The numerator a²+b² is 9+4; the denominator ab is −2.

questions.stem: The roots of x² − 5x + 3 = 0 are a and b. What is (a − 1)(b − 1) + (a + 1)(b + 1)?
questions.explanation: Expanding the two products cancels the terms involving a + b and leaves 2ab + 2. Since ab = 3, the result is 8.

questions.stem: The roots of x²−6x+4=0 are p and q. What is (p−1)(q−1)?
questions.explanation: Expanding gives pq−(p+q)+1=4−6+1.

questions.stem: The roots of x²−3x+1=0 are u,v. What is u³+v³?
questions.explanation: Subtract 3uv(u+v) from (u+v)³ to remove the cross terms.

questions.stem: If a and b are the roots of 2x²+7x−3=0, what is 1/(a+2)+1/(b+2)?
questions.explanation: The numerator is a+b+4=1/2 and the denominator is ab+2(a+b)+4=−9/2.

questions.stem: Let a and b be the real roots of x² − sx + 4 = 0. If a + 1/a + b + 1/b = 15, what is s?
questions.explanation: The reciprocal sum is (a + b)/(ab) = s/4, so the full sum is 5s/4. Equating that to 15 gives s = 12, which does give distinct real roots.

questions.stem: A monic quadratic has roots whose sum is 8 and whose product is 12. What is the sum of their positive square roots?
questions.explanation: Both roots are positive, and squaring the requested sum gives 8+2√12.

questions.stem: The two distinct positive roots α, β of x² − 9x + 14 = 0 are transformed by f(x) = 1/(x + 5). What is f(α) + f(β)?
questions.explanation:
By the coefficients, α + β = 9 and αβ = 14. The common denominator is αβ + 5(α + β) + 25; the numerator is α + β + 10. Substitute without solving the quadratic.

Answer: 19/84.

questions.stem: The two distinct positive roots α, β of x² − 18x + 80 = 0 are transformed by f(x) = 1/(x + 7). What is f(α) + f(β)?
questions.explanation:
By the coefficients, α + β = 18 and αβ = 80. The common denominator is αβ + 7(α + β) + 49; the numerator is α + β + 14. Substitute without solving the quadratic.

Answer: 32/255.

questions.stem: A rectangle has its base on the x-axis and its upper vertices on y=9−x². Its area is largest for which positive x-coordinate of the upper right vertex?
questions.explanation: The area is 2x(9−x²) for 0≤x≤3, with derivative 18−6x². It changes from positive to negative at √3.

questions.stem: A right triangle has perpendicular sides 6 and 8. An inscribed rectangle has two sides lying along those sides and its opposite corner on the hypotenuse. What is its largest possible area?
questions.explanation: For width w along the side of length 6, the height is 8−4w/3. The product peaks at w=3 and height 4.

questions.stem: A rectangle with base on the x-axis has upper corners on y = 12 − 2|x|. What is its height when the area is maximised?
questions.explanation: If its half-width is t, equal heights on the sloping sides put the corners at ±t. The area is 2t(12 − 2t) = 36 − 4(t − 3)², maximised at t = 3. The height is then 6.

questions.stem: An axis-aligned rectangle is centred at the origin with all corners on x²/9+y²/4=1. What is its area if its length and height are in the ratio 3:2?
questions.explanation: The positive vertex is (3t,2t), with 2t²=1. The area is 24t²=12.

questions.stem: An axis-aligned rectangle has upper vertices on y=4−|x| and its base on y=0. If its area is 6, what is the sum of the two possible widths?
questions.explanation: For half-width x the equation is 2x(4−x)=6. The half-width roots sum to 4, so the widths sum to 8.

questions.stem: A rectangle inscribed in a circle of radius 5 has one side of length 6. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: The diagonal is a diameter of length 10. The other side is √(100−36)=8.

questions.stem: A rectangle has its lower corners at (−t, 0) and (t, 0) and its upper corners on y = 10 − x². For t > 0, what is its perimeter when the height is twice its width?
questions.explanation: The width is 2t, so 10 − t² = 4t, or (t + 2)² = 14. The positive half-width is √14 − 2. The perimeter is 2(2t + 4t) = 12(√14 − 2).

questions.stem: A rectangle is inscribed in a semicircle of radius 6, with its base along the diameter and both upper corners on the arc. What is the maximum area?
questions.explanation: For half-width x and height y, x²+y²=36. Thus 2xy≤36 by (x−y)²≥0, with equality at x=y.

questions.stem: The graph y = 7 − |x − 2| is above the x-axis on a symmetric interval. A rectangle has base on the x-axis, vertical sides at x = 2 − t and x = 2 + t, and both upper corners on the graph. If its area is maximal, what is its area?
questions.explanation:
Here 0 ≤ t ≤ 7; the rectangle has width 2t and height 7 − t. Its area is 2t(7 − t) = 49/2 − 2(t − 7/2)², maximised when the square is zero.

Answer: 49/2.

questions.stem: The graph y = 13 − |x − 10| is above the x-axis on a symmetric interval. A rectangle has base on the x-axis, vertical sides at x = 10 − t and x = 10 + t, and both upper corners on the graph. If its area is maximal, what is its area?
questions.explanation:
Here 0 ≤ t ≤ 13; the rectangle has width 2t and height 13 − t. Its area is 2t(13 − t) = 169/2 − 2(t − 13/2)², maximised when the square is zero.

Answer: 169/2.

questions.stem: Three real observations have mean 10, median 9 and range 8. What is their smallest value?
questions.explanation: If the smallest is m, the largest is m+8. The sum 2m+17 is 30.

questions.stem: Four distinct integers have range 5 and mean 8. What is the least possible value of their maximum?
questions.explanation: A maximum of 9 forces a minimum of 4 and sum at most 4+7+8+9=28. The set {5,8,9,10} has sum 32.

questions.stem: Three distinct positive integers have mean 8 and range 6. What is the largest possible median?
questions.explanation: If the smallest number is a, the largest is a + 6 and the middle is 18 − 2a. Being strictly below a + 6 requires a > 4. The least possible a is 5, giving the valid list 5, 8, 11. Larger a decrease the median, so the answer is 8.

questions.stem: Five numbers have mean 4 and range 10. After replacing each x by 7−2x, what is the new range?
questions.explanation: The transformation reverses order and multiplies every difference in magnitude by 2.

questions.stem: Two additional observations equal to the original mean are added to a nonconstant data set. Which statement must hold?
options: The variance about the mean decreases.
questions.explanation: The added observations lie between the extremes. The mean stays fixed; the same positive sum of squared deviations is now divided by more observations. The median can change, for example starting with 0, 0, 9.

questions.stem: The numbers a, b, c have mean 5. The numbers a+1, b+3, c−1 have mean 6 and are all equal. What was the original range?
questions.explanation: The new values must all be 6, so the originals were 5, 3, 7.

questions.stem: Four distinct integers have range 8. How much larger is the mean of the largest three than the mean of the smallest three?
questions.explanation: The two middle entries appear in both sums and cancel when they are subtracted. The difference between the sums is just the greatest entry minus the least, which is 8, so the mean difference is 8/3.

questions.stem: Three integers have median 7, mean 7 and range less than 8. How many distinct ordered triples in nondecreasing order are possible?
questions.explanation: The extremes have sum 14, so they are 7−d and 7+d with integer d=0,1,2,3.

questions.stem: Three different integers are selected from 1 through 15. Each selection is unordered. In how many selections is the difference between the greatest and least integers exactly 5?
questions.explanation:
The least element a ranges from 1 to 10; then the greatest is fixed at a + 5. There are 4 choices strictly between them for the remaining number.

Answer: 40.

questions.stem: Three different integers are selected from 1 through 10. Each selection is unordered. In how many selections is the difference between the greatest and least integers exactly 7?
questions.explanation:
The least element a ranges from 1 to 3; then the greatest is fixed at a + 7. There are 6 choices strictly between them for the remaining number.

Answer: 18.

questions.stem: For positive n, which condition is necessary but not sufficient for 18 to divide 4n?
questions.explanation: The original condition is equivalent to 9 dividing n. A multiple of 9 is a multiple of 3 but 3 itself fails. The stronger multiples 18 and 27 are not necessary, and n=9 rules out the other choices.

questions.stem: Which pair of integer conditions is equivalent?
options: 6 and 9 both divide n ↔ 54 divides n
questions.explanation: The factor 6 supplies one factor of 2, and divisibility by 4 needs one more. Counterexamples to equivalence are 18, 2, 6, and 2 for the other pairs.

questions.stem: For positive integers a and b, let P mean 4 divides a² and Q mean 4 divides ab. Which correctly describes P as a condition for Q?
options: Neither, and they cannot both hold
questions.explanation: P holds for (a, b) = (2, 1) without Q; Q holds for (1, 4) without P. The pair (2, 2) satisfies both.

questions.stem: A positive integer m is such that divisibility by 12 implies divisibility by m, and divisibility by m implies divisibility by 2. How many m are possible?
questions.explanation: The first implication requires m to divide 12 (test n=12); the second requires m to be even (test n=m). This gives 2,4,6,12.

questions.stem: Which integer n disproves the claim that if 24 divides n² then 24 divides n?
questions.explanation: At 12 the square is 144, a multiple of 24, whereas 12 itself is not. At 6,8,10 the square fails the premise, and 24 satisfies the conclusion.

questions.stem: If 35 divides ab and 5 does not divide a, which must be true for positive integers a,b?
questions.explanation: Prime 5 divides ab but not a, so divides b. Examples (7,5) and (1,35) distinguish the other proposed conclusions.

questions.stem: Which statement is necessary, but not sufficient, for the product of two positive integers to be divisible by 8?
options: At least one integer is even.
The sum of the integers is even.
questions.explanation: A product of two odd integers is odd, so at least one factor must be even. But the product 2·3 is not divisible by 8. The pair (1, 8) rules out both integers even or an even sum as necessary, and (2, 4) rules out exactly one even integer or an individual multiple of 8 as necessary.

questions.stem: Which single statement is sufficient for 6 to divide an integer n?
questions.explanation: If 12 divides n², both prime factors 2 and 3 divide n; thus so does 6. For the other choices use n=5,3,2,3 respectively.

questions.stem:
Let x be a positive integer. P: 5 divides x. Q: 30 divides x.

Which describes P relative to Q?
options: Neither, but both can hold together
Neither, and they cannot both hold
questions.explanation: P ⇒ Q exactly when 30 divides 5: test the least positive multiple 5 itself. Q ⇒ P exactly when 5 divides 30: test 30 itself. The product 150 shows that both can hold. The two implications are respectively false and true.

questions.stem:
Let x be a positive integer. P: 24 divides x. Q: 9 divides x.

Which describes P relative to Q?
options: Neither, but both can hold together
Neither, and they cannot both hold
questions.explanation: P ⇒ Q exactly when 9 divides 24: test the least positive multiple 24 itself. Q ⇒ P exactly when 24 divides 9: test 9 itself. The product 216 shows that both can hold. The two implications are respectively false and false.

questions.stem: For integer n, which condition is equivalent to 3n+1>15?
questions.explanation: The real bound is n>14/3; the first allowed integer is 5.

questions.stem: An integer n satisfies n(n+1)<20. What is the difference between the largest and smallest possible n?
questions.explanation: Equality occurs at −5 and 4, so the integer extremes strictly between them are −4 and 3.

questions.stem: Let n be a positive integer. Which bound is necessary and sufficient for n² + n ≤ 30?
questions.explanation: The expression n(n + 1) increases strictly over positive integers. Its value at 5 is 30 and at 6 is 42, so the largest allowed n is 5.

questions.stem: Which integer bound is necessary but not sufficient for n²≤16?
questions.explanation: The admissible integers run from −4 to 4. The lower bound is necessary, but n=5 satisfies it without satisfying the square bound.

questions.stem: If 1≤n≤20 and n is an integer, when does n/4 round to 3 to the nearest integer, with ties rounded up?
questions.explanation: Round to 3 exactly on [2.5,3.5), giving integer n=10 through 13.

questions.stem: What is the smallest positive integer n for which at least half of {1,…,n} are greater than 5?
questions.explanation: Once n exceeds 5 the proportion is (n−5)/n, which is at least one half exactly when n≥10.

questions.stem: Let n be a positive integer. The conditions n² > 20 and n > c are equivalent. Which of the following could be c?
questions.explanation: The square inequality is true exactly for n ≥ 5. To include 5 and exclude 4, c must satisfy 4 ≤ c < 5. Only 9/2 is in that interval.

questions.stem: Which integer n satisfies exactly one of n≥−1 and 2n<5?
questions.explanation: The conditions overlap on the integers −1 to 2; n=3 satisfies the first alone.

questions.stem:
Let x be an integer. P: |x − 4| < 6. Q: (x − 4)² ≤ 36.

Which describes P relative to Q?
options: Neither, and they cannot both hold
Neither, but both can hold together
questions.explanation: For integer x, P is the interval [-1, 9] while Q is [-2, 10]. P ⇒ Q if the first interval is contained in the second; Q ⇒ P if the containment is reversed. Both intervals contain 4.

questions.stem:
Let x be an integer. P: |x − 2| < 3. Q: (x − 2)² ≤ 25.

Which describes P relative to Q?
options: Neither, and they cannot both hold
Neither, but both can hold together
questions.explanation: For integer x, P is the interval [0, 4] while Q is [-3, 7]. P ⇒ Q if the first interval is contained in the second; Q ⇒ P if the containment is reversed. Both intervals contain 2.

questions.stem: An integer n has remainder 2 on division by 5. What is the least positive such n with remainder 1 on division by 4?
questions.explanation: The candidates begin 2,7,12,17. Their residues modulo 4 are 2,3,0,1.

questions.stem: An integer leaves remainder 1 on division by 4 and remainder 2 on division by 6. What can it leave on division by 12?
questions.explanation: The first condition makes the integer odd; the second makes it even.

questions.stem: A number n leaves remainder 2 on division by 4 and remainder 1 on division by 3. What remainder does n leave on division by 12?
questions.explanation: The candidates modulo 12 from the first condition are 2, 6 and 10. Of these, only 10 has remainder 1 on division by 3.

questions.stem: If n≡2 modulo 6, which remainder is impossible for n² on division by 9?
questions.explanation: Modulo 9 the admissible residues of n are 2,5,8. Their squares leave 4,7,1 respectively.

questions.stem: On division by 7, m leaves remainder 4 and n leaves remainder 5. What is the remainder of m²−n²?
questions.explanation: The difference is congruent to 16−25=−9, which leaves 5 modulo 7.

questions.stem: For how many n from 100 to 119 inclusive is the remainder of n on division by 4 equal to its remainder on division by 5?
questions.explanation: The 20 consecutive integers cover a cycle. Equal residues occur only at common remainders 0,1,2,3, each reached once.

questions.stem: An integer leaves remainder 2 when divided by 6. Which can be its remainder when divided by 9?
questions.explanation: Modulo 18 the first condition allows 2, 8 and 14. These reduce to 2, 8 and 5 modulo 9, and each occurs.

questions.stem: If a positive integer is one more than a multiple of 3 and two more than a multiple of 5, by how much does it differ from the next larger such integer?
questions.explanation: The gap must be a positive multiple of both 3 and 5; adding 15 preserves both remainders.

questions.stem:
Let x be an integer. P: x − 19 is divisible by 2. Q: x − 19 is divisible by 2.

Which describes P relative to Q?
options: Neither, and they cannot both hold
Neither, but both can hold together
questions.explanation: Subtract the two differences: their difference is 0. If it is divisible by 2, the conditions describe exactly the same residue class. If it is not divisible by 2, the classes are disjoint, and x = 19 and x = 19 witness the two failed implications.

questions.stem:
Let x be an integer. P: x − 19 is divisible by 4. Q: x − 19 is divisible by 4.

Which describes P relative to Q?
options: Neither, and they cannot both hold
Neither, but both can hold together
questions.explanation: Subtract the two differences: their difference is 0. If it is divisible by 4, the conditions describe exactly the same residue class. If it is not divisible by 4, the classes are disjoint, and x = 19 and x = 19 witness the two failed implications.

questions.stem: Which condition is the negation of “at least one of a,b is greater than 3”?
options: At least one is at most 3.
questions.explanation: To deny that either exceeds 3 requires keeping each at or below 3, including equality.

questions.stem: Which statement negates “for every x in [0,1], f(x)>0”?
questions.explanation: One failure of the strict inequality inside the specified domain is enough; that failure includes equality.

questions.stem: What is the negation of “There are two different real numbers a and b with f(a) = f(b)”?
options: There are no real numbers a and b with f(a) = f(b).
No real numbers have the same input.
For every a and b, f(a) ≠ f(b).
For any two different real numbers a and b, f(a) ≠ f(b).
For every real number a there exists a different b with f(a) ≠ f(b).
questions.explanation: Negating an existence claim gives a universal one. For each pair of different inputs, the equality must fail. The restriction that the inputs differ matters: f(a) always equals itself.

questions.stem: What is the negation of “a<b<c” for reals a,b,c?
questions.explanation: The chain is a conjunction. It fails whenever at least one comparison fails, at equality or in the reverse order.

questions.stem: If |x−2|<5 is false, which x are possible?
questions.explanation: The original condition means −3<x<7. Its complement includes both endpoints and everything outside them.

questions.stem: Which statement is false exactly when x>2 and y<5?
questions.explanation: The requested statement is the complement of an intersection. Either x≤2 or y≥5 negates one of its two conditions.

questions.stem: A claim states that at least one of the three numbers a, b and c is smaller than each of the other two. Which triple refutes this claim?
questions.explanation: A unique strictly smallest number exists unless the minimum is shared. In the fourth triple, 1 is shared; in the others there is one strictly smallest entry.

questions.stem: Which pair makes “both x² and y² are strictly below 4” false, while leaving x and y nonnegative and at most 2?
questions.explanation: The y-coordinate 2 gives equality with the bound, negating the strict comparison. The first three satisfy both square bounds, and (3,0) is outside the extra restrictions.

questions.stem: Which statement is the formal negation of: ‘For every integer n, if 5 divides n then n² ≤ 16’?
options: Every integer n divisible by 5 has n² > 16.
Some integer n is divisible by 5 and n² ≤ 16.
Every integer n with n² ≥ 16 is divisible by 5.
Some integer n is divisible by 5 and n² > 16.
Some integer n is not divisible by 5 and n² > 16.
questions.explanation: Negating ‘for every’ gives ‘there exists’. The implication fails only if n is divisible by 5 but the conclusion fails; the complement of ≥ is < and the complement of ≤ is >. Negate the form of the assertion; no particular witness is needed to write the negation.

questions.stem: Which statement is the formal negation of: ‘For every integer n, if 5 divides n then n² ≥ 121’?
options: Every integer n divisible by 5 has n² < 121.
Every integer n with n² ≤ 121 is divisible by 5.
Some integer n is divisible by 5 and n² < 121.
Some integer n is not divisible by 5 and n² < 121.
Some integer n is divisible by 5 and n² ≥ 121.
questions.explanation: Negating ‘for every’ gives ‘there exists’. The implication fails only if n is divisible by 5 but the conclusion fails; the complement of ≥ is < and the complement of ≤ is >. Negate the form of the assertion; no particular witness is needed to write the negation.

questions.stem: It is given that if x>1 then f(x)<0. Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: Negating the conclusion gives f(x)≥0, which forces the premise x>1 to fail. Nothing excludes x=1.

questions.stem: Every integer whose cube is odd is odd. Which statement expresses the contrapositive?
options: If n is odd, n³ is odd.
If n is even, n³ is even.
If n³ is even, n is even.
If n is odd, n³ is even.
At least one of n and n³ is even.
questions.explanation: The premise is about n³. The contrapositive starts with failure of the conclusion, so starts with even n.

questions.stem: Consider the implication “If f has a repeated root, then f and its derivative have a common root.” Which statement is its contrapositive?
options: If f and its derivative have a common root, then f has a repeated root.
If f has no repeated root, then f and its derivative have no common root.
If f and its derivative have no common root, then f has no repeated root.
If f has no repeated root, then f has no roots at all.
If f has a repeated root, then its derivative has a repeated root.
questions.explanation: The contrapositive of P implies Q is not Q implies not P. In particular, neither reversing nor negating only the original implication gives its contrapositive.

questions.stem: For any a on a list, if a divides 30 and a divides 42, then a divides 6. The number b belongs to the list but does not divide 6. What follows?
options: b divides exactly one of 30 and 42.
b fails to divide at least one of 30 and 42.
questions.explanation: Since the conclusion fails, the conjunction in the hypothesis must fail. Both divisibilities can fail, for example if b=5+6.

questions.stem: When P is false, Q must be true. Which other rule has exactly the same allowed truth assignments?
options: If Q is true, P is false.
If Q is false, P is true.
If P is true, Q is true.
If P is true, Q is false.
If Q is false, P is false.
questions.explanation: The only forbidden assignment is that both P and Q are false, so a false Q forces true P.

questions.stem: If f(a)=f(b), then a=b. Which is the contrapositive?
questions.explanation: Reverse the order of the conditional and negate both equalities.

questions.stem: Every number in a set T that lies strictly between 0 and 1 is rational. What must be true of each irrational number in T?
options: It is outside the open interval (0, 1).
